source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Tree to ca. 30 m tall as printed in 1999 flora; unusually high figure requires independent corroboration
morphology_documented.bark: Grayish, approximately smooth, peeling in thin layers (species key)
morphology_documented.leaves: Alternate, simple, entire (genus); 2–5 cm long, nearly sessile and persistently pubescent (species key and treatment)
morphology_documented.flowers: Axillary, drooping, urn- to bell-shaped, imperfectly unisexual; genus: usually 4-merous pale corolla, inferior staminate flowers smaller than pistillate
morphology_documented.fruit: Black berry ca. 2 cm diameter, pubescent ovary and fruit, edible when ripe
morphology_documented.habitat: Rocky woods, slopes, open areas, streams

source_scope_note: Species vs genus/key-level characters distinguished in text; no undocumented characters inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Source printed height 'to ca. 30 m' differs from common field descriptions; exact value preserved but flagged rather than silently normalized
Species key separates American persimmon by glabrous mature leaves, larger fruits, dark furrowed bark
preservation: Additive research record, existing species cards, original media, credits and galleries unchanged
